cards.text: Jerusalem has fallen, and God's people have been carried off to Babylon (2 Kings 25:8-11). This psalm's writer isn't named and speaks as "we," one of the captives telling what it was like there. It opens by the rivers of Babylon, where they sat and remembered Zion, in Jerusalem.

cards.question: By the rivers of Babylon, God's people remember Zion. What do they do there?

cards.text: There on the willows, they hang up their harps. I think I know a little about going quiet, friend: in the junk drawer I went a good while without one single joke, and now look at me, I can't STOP.

cards.question: The captives hang their harps on the willows in Babylon. What was going on there?

answers.text: Their captors demanded songs of joy
Their harps had all broken strings
Their leaders told them to stay silent

cards.question: The captors don't want just any song. They want the captives to sing a song about Babylon.

cards.text: Picture your boss catching you on your worst day and shouting, "Come on, tell everybody something FUN!" Then the psalm asks a question of its own.

cards.question: The psalm asks how God's people can sing a song of the LORD in a ___ land.

cards.text: Now the "we" turns into "I." The writer speaks straight to Jerusalem, like the city could hear every word.

cards.question: The writer speaks to Jerusalem and starts with an "if." What is that "if" about?

cards.text: The writer says, "If I forget you, O Jerusalem, may my right hand cease to function." And then, "May my tongue cling to the roof of my mouth…"

cards.question: The writer speaks of exalting Jerusalem as the writer's greatest joy.

cards.text: Then the writer turns to the LORD and brings up the sons of Edom, the people who came from Esau (Genesis 36:9). It goes back to the day Jerusalem fell.

cards.question: On the day Jerusalem fell, what were the sons of Edom saying about the city?

answers.text: Tear it down to its foundations

cards.question: The writer asks the LORD to forget what the sons of Edom said the day Jerusalem fell.

cards.text: There's that word again: remember. Now the writer turns to Babylon itself: "O Daughter of Babylon, doomed to destruction…"

cards.question: The writer says the one who repays Babylon is ___.
The writer calls the one who repays Babylon blessed. Repays Babylon in what way?

answers.text: As Babylon has done to them
With a fair trial for its king

cards.text: Then comes the last line, and it's the hardest one in the psalm: "Blessed is he who seizes your infants and dashes them against the rocks." That's where the psalm ends, friend, and it doesn't tidy anything up.
